_comment: THE PUBLIC SURFACE, DESCRIBED ONCE, FOR MACHINE READERS.
This file is the single source of truth for the three AI-facing artifacts:
out/llms.txt        written by scripts/generate-llms-txt.js at build time
out/llms-full.txt   same generator, with the descriptions inlined
/mcp                amplify/functions/ai/mcp-server reads it from its own zip
THE `pages` ARRAY IS GENERATED. DO NOT HAND-EDIT IT.
node scripts/generate-public-pages.js          rewrites it from the tree
node scripts/generate-public-pages.js --check   fails if it is stale (runs in CI)
It is derived from PUBLIC_EXACT in scripts/generate-sitemap.js, PUBLIC_PAGE_META and the
render chains in src/pages/_app.tsx, src/content/products.ts, src/content/customerservice.ts and
src/content/legal/, plus the presence of a real file under src/pages/. Add a page, delete a
page or reword its description and this array follows on the next build. The one field no
scan can infer is `group` - that is a positioning decision - so a new public route with no
group is a hard build failure naming the line to add rather than a guess.
Everything ELSE in this file is hand-written and the generator preserves it untouched:
site, groups, ai_surface, usage_terms.
IT IS DERIVED, NOT AUTHORITATIVE, AND THAT DISTINCTION IS LOAD-BEARING.
The render allowlist is PUBLIC_PAGE_META plus the isPublic chain in src/pages/_app.tsx;
the crawl allowlist is PUBLIC_EXACT in scripts/generate-sitemap.js. Those two decide what
actually exists. This file only describes it. src/test/PublicAiSurface.test.ts fails the
build when the three drift apart, because the failure mode is silent and ugly in both
directions: a page listed here but missing from _app.tsx serves the staff sign-in shell at
HTTP 200, and a page missing here is simply invisible to every agent that reads llms.txt or
calls the MCP server.
WHY A JSON FILE RATHER THAN IMPORTING _app.tsx. The generator is Node, the MCP server is
Python, and _app.tsx executes Amplify.configure at module scope. A shared data file is the
only form all three can read without one of them booting the frontend.
The 889 blog posts are NOT listed here. They change on a content publish rather than a code
change, and the generator fetches them from /api/seo-tools/blog-public exactly as
generate-sitemap.js already does.

_comment: THERE IS NO human_page KEY ANY MORE, and its absence is a decision rather than an omission.
/llm/ was an HTML page that described this endpoint in prose. It was retired on 2026-09-30:
a documentation page for a machine interface is a fifth place the tool list, the protocol
versions and the limits had to be kept in step, and the audience that needed it can get a
better answer from the endpoint itself. `initialize` returns an `instructions` string,
`tools/list` returns the tools with their schemas, and get_site_summary returns this whole
block. Everything the page said now lives here and in /llms.txt, which is where a reader
arriving from robots.txt actually lands. /llm and /llm/ DO NOT REDIRECT - they answer 404
through the `/<*>` catch-all. There was a 301 to /llms.txt for a few hours on the day of
the retirement; the owner removed it, so the 404 is deliberate. See the note where the
RETIRED entry used to be in scripts/provision_legacy_redirects.py, which records what the
301 would have bought and what was traded away.
mcp_tools MUST equal READ_ONLY_TOOLS in amplify/functions/ai/mcp/handler.py, asserted in
both directions by src/test/PublicAiSurface.test.ts. `summary` is prose for a reader and is
deliberately not the handler's `description`, which is written to instruct a model.

ai_surface.note: The MCP endpoint is read-only and unauthenticated. It exposes the public pages and the published blog corpus, and nothing else. That is not a permission setting: the capability to act is absent from the handler, and its test suite asserts the tool list against a frozen allowlist so a tool with a side effect cannot be added quietly. A GET returns 405 by design - the server is stateless and offers no SSE stream, which the specification names as the explicit alternative.

usage_terms: The public pages and published blog posts on this site may be read, quoted with attribution, and cited by AI assistants and answer engines.
Attribute to WECARE.DIGITAL and link the page you drew from.
Do not present generated text as a statement by WECARE.DIGITAL, and do not infer prices, turnaround times, medical, legal or financial advice that a page does not state.
Bharat Rx does not retail medicines. Do not describe it as a pharmacy.
Anything under /workspace/ or /api/ is operational surface, not content. It is disallowed in robots.txt and is not covered by this permission.
